paragraphs: Training robot models on diverse demonstrations becomes difficult when their observations leave out information needed to interpret actions. The paper describes two sources of inconsistency: mismatched coordinate systems and ambiguous states. Similar-looking inputs can therefore correspond to different actions, making the relationship the model must learn more scattered and reducing pretraining efficiency.

4D-VLA enriches visual inputs with depth and time through sequences of RGB-D images. This helps align the robot’s coordinate system with the surrounding scene and gives the model information about how the situation develops. A complementary memory bank sampling strategy selects informative historical frames. Together, these components aim to improve spatial and temporal reasoning while keeping additional training overhead small.

Experiments in simulation and on real robots report substantially higher success rates than OpenVLA. The authors also introduce MV-Bench to test spatial perception and generalization to unfamiliar views. Strong results there support the value of making geometry and history explicit when learning from varied robot data.
neurips-2025-4d-vla-spatiotemporal-visio.tldr: 4D-VLA adds depth and historical observations to robot pretraining, improving action learning and generalization across views.

paragraphs: Search can supply a language model with relevant information, but complex questions also require deciding what to retrieve and connecting evidence across steps. AceSearcher addresses these linked difficulties by training one model to alternate between two cooperating roles: decomposing a question into smaller queries and solving it using retrieved context.

Training begins with supervised examples covering search, reasoning, and decomposition. Reinforcement fine-tuning then rewards final answer accuracy, allowing the two roles to improve together without intermediate annotations for that stage. This connects the usefulness of question decomposition to the quality of the eventual answer, rather than evaluating the retrieval and reasoning processes only in isolation.

Across ten datasets spanning three reasoning-intensive tasks, AceSearcher reports an average exact match improvement of 7.6% over leading baselines. On document-level finance reasoning, its 32-billion-parameter version matches DeepSeek-V3 with less than 5% of its parameters. Smaller versions also often beat search-augmented models up to nine times larger, supporting the effectiveness of the cooperative training approach.
neurips-2025-acesearcher-bootstrapping-r.tldr: AceSearcher trains one language model to cooperate with itself as a query decomposer and evidence-based solver, improving search-intensive reasoning.

paragraphs: A reconstructed CT image can score well on common image similarity measures while still missing important anatomy. The paper focuses on sparse-view reconstruction, where small or thin structures are especially vulnerable. Measures such as SSIM and PSNR emphasize image fidelity but can fail to reflect whether anatomical structures have been preserved completely.

The authors introduce anatomy-aware metrics that assess completeness across large organs, small organs, intestines, and vessels. They then use this perspective to build CARE, a reconstruction enhancement framework. CARE adds structural penalties during training so that preserving significant anatomy becomes part of the learning objective, connecting the proposed evaluation criteria to an actionable improvement method.

CARE can be integrated into analytical, implicit, and generative reconstruction approaches. Across the methods studied, reported completeness improvements reach up to 32% for large organs, 22% for small organs, 40% for intestines, and 36% for vessels. These are category-specific maxima, showing that explicitly evaluating and encouraging anatomical preservation can improve aspects of reconstruction that conventional metrics overlook.
neurips-2025-are-pixel-wise-metrics-reli.tldr: Anatomy-aware metrics and CARE training penalties improve the structural completeness of CT reconstructions beyond what conventional image metrics capture.

paragraphs: Video-language models may encounter an ongoing stream of changing scenes and tasks, rather than a fixed dataset. Updating only a small fraction of their parameters reduces adaptation costs, but creates difficulties: new learning can erase earlier knowledge, and updates for different tasks can conflict. Bisecle addresses these problems in continual video understanding.

Its design draws inspiration from memory binding and pattern separation in the hippocampus. A multi-directional supervision module captures more relationships between video and language, while contrastive prompt learning separates task-specific knowledge. The two mechanisms serve complementary purposes: linking information across modalities and keeping distinct task information from interfering during continued adaptation.

Evaluations on several video question-answering benchmarks show reduced forgetting and better generalization across tasks. The findings support combining richer cross-modal supervision with explicit separation of task knowledge when only limited parameters can be updated. The contribution is a way to improve memory retention and transfer within the computational constraints of adapting large multimodal models.
neurips-2025-bisecle-binding-and-separat.tldr: Bisecle combines cross-modal binding with task-specific separation to reduce forgetting during parameter-efficient continual video-language learning.

paragraphs: Zero-shot black-box optimization asks a pretrained optimizer to solve unfamiliar problems without task-specific tuning. Such a model must recognize useful problem features and turn them into strategies for generating candidate solutions. The paper organizes this challenge around three components: task representations, strategy representations, and the learned mapping connecting the two.

EPOM improves each part of that pipeline. A tokenizer based on cross-attention builds richer task representations, while deformable attention increases the diversity of optimization strategies. A differentiable crossover mechanism replaces non-differentiable operations to make training more stable. These changes target weak representations, rigid candidate-generation strategies, and unstable learning identified in existing pretrained optimization models.

The authors report better generalization, faster convergence, and more reliable performance on zero-shot black-box optimization. The approach matters because deployment on new tasks depends on both recognizing unfamiliar structure and responding with a suitable strategy. EPOM treats these abilities, together with training stability, as connected design problems for an optimizer intended to transfer without additional tuning.
neurips-2025-enhancing-zero-shot-black-b.tldr: EPOM improves pretrained black-box optimizers through richer task features, more flexible strategies, and differentiable training operations.

paragraphs: Learning systems often optimize a convenient surrogate loss instead of the target loss that defines success. A surrogate regret bound describes how excess error on the training objective translates into excess error on the target objective. A linear bound preserves the convergence rate through this translation, making it especially valuable when the surrogate is efficient to optimize.

The paper constructs convex, smooth surrogate losses with linear regret bounds for arbitrary discrete target losses, provided they are paired with a tailored prediction link. This challenges the presumed tradeoff between smoothness and lossless regret transfer. The construction uses Fenchel–Young losses generated through an infimal convolution combining generalized negentropy with the target Bayes risk.

That construction supplies smoothness while retaining a linear relationship between surrogate and target regret. It also yields a consistent estimator of the underlying class probabilities. The result establishes that favorable optimization properties and strong statistical transfer can coexist in this construction; the prediction link is part of the guarantee, alongside the surrogate itself.
neurips-2025-establishing-linear-surroga.tldr: A convex-analysis construction yields smooth convex surrogates with linear regret transfer for arbitrary discrete target losses when paired with tailored prediction links.

paragraphs: Air quality forecasting must describe how pollutant concentrations change across both space and time. The paper identifies a combined challenge for existing models: capturing these complicated dynamics while maintaining spatial continuity in the predicted pollutant distribution. CTENet addresses the problem by bringing a chemical transport equation into a neural forecasting framework.

Specifically, it embeds the advection-diffusion-reaction equation within a physics-informed neural network. The equation represents pollutant transport, spreading, and reactions, giving the learned model a physical description of how concentrations evolve. An Eulerian representation describes that evolution at spatial locations. This connects the forecasting task to the processes governing pollutant distributions rather than relying solely on learned statistical relationships.

Experiments on two real-world datasets report improvements over state-of-the-art baselines. The stated RMSE improvements are 45.8% on the USA dataset and 21.0% on the China dataset. These results support chemical transport information as a useful component of neural air quality forecasting across the two evaluated settings.
neurips-2025-eulerian-neural-network-inf.tldr: CTENet embeds chemical transport physics into a neural network and reports substantial air quality forecasting improvements on USA and China datasets.

paragraphs: Event cameras offer high dynamic range, but structured-light measurements can still fail on strongly reflective or absorptive surfaces. Some regions produce cluttered events while others produce too few, degrading the recovered 3D structure. The paper develops an HDR measurement framework specifically for these event-based systems, addressing both illumination coding and reconstruction.

A multi-contrast coding strategy supports surfaces with different reflectance levels. During stereo matching, the method estimates a confidence map and uses it to weight feature fusion, reducing interference between frames. A confidence propagation volume further represents matching information while suppressing that interference. These components make the reconstruction process sensitive to how trustworthy the observed information is.

The work also supplies an event-based structured-light simulator, an HDR dataset, and a real-world benchmark with ground truth. Tests on synthetic and real measurements support the confidence-driven approach and report accurate reconstruction under extreme conditions. The contribution combines a measurement method with resources for evaluating the difficult lighting and reflectance cases it targets.
neurips-2025-event-based-hdr-structured-.tldr: Multi-contrast illumination and confidence-aware matching improve event-based 3D reconstruction on surfaces that produce excessive or insufficient events.

paragraphs: Low prices for training data can affect the future quality of the market supplying it. This paper models interactions between language model builders and human annotators, examining how exploitative pricing can push high-quality sellers to leave. Its theoretical and empirical analysis links that departure to poorer data and weaker long-term model performance.

Fairshare bases payments on data valuation: an assessment of each piece of data’s contribution. The mechanism aims to align buyer and seller incentives so that supplying valuable data remains worthwhile. Within the proposed theoretical framework, the authors show mutually optimal outcomes that maximize long-term buyer utility and seller profit while maintaining participation.

Experiments train open-source language models on tasks involving mathematics, medical diagnosis, and physical reasoning. Fairshare increases seller earnings, sustains high-quality data supply, and improves buyer performance per dollar and long-term welfare. These findings connect compensation to model-building economics: maintaining participation by valuable contributors can benefit buyers as well as the people producing the data.
neurips-2025-fairshare-data-pricing-via-.tldr: Fairshare prices training data by its contribution, aligning seller compensation with sustained data quality and long-term buyer value.

paragraphs: Generating human motion from language requires producing plausible sequences while managing the substantial cost of diffusion models. The paper identifies expensive training and inference, along with scalability constraints associated with U-Net designs, as obstacles. FlashMo addresses efficiency through frequency-aware sparsity, pruning low-frequency tokens without requiring custom computational kernels.

The work also introduces MotionSiT, a scalable diffusion transformer that treats joint and temporal structure through a factorized interpolant. Its construction uses geodesics on the space of 3D rotations, giving joint rotations a geometrically principled generation process. The overall approach therefore combines reduced token computation with an architecture designed around the structure of articulated motion.

Experiments on MotionHub V2, HumanML3D, and KIT-ML report improvements in motion quality, efficiency, and scalability. Relative to a state-of-the-art one-step distillation baseline, FlashMo reduces inference time by 12.9% and FID by 34.1%. These results show that the reported efficiency gains accompany improved generation quality in the evaluated comparison.
neurips-2025-flashmo-geometric-interpola.tldr: FlashMo combines frequency-aware token pruning with geometrically structured motion generation to improve speed, quality, and scalability.

paragraphs: Editing an object described in language requires understanding which object is meant, locating its boundaries, and generating the requested visual change. The paper argues that existing approaches often separate these responsibilities across isolated segmentation and generation components. FOCUS integrates them into one vision-language framework so that object-aware perception and controllable editing are learned together.

A dual-branch visual encoder captures both the overall meaning of an image and detailed spatial information. A MoVQGAN-based tokenizer supplies discrete visual tokens for generation. During progressive, multi-stage training, segmentation masks are jointly optimized and also used as spatial prompts for a diffusion decoder, connecting object localization directly to the generation process.

Experiments cover multimodal understanding, referring segmentation, and controllable image generation. The authors report strong performance across these three tasks, supporting the joint optimization of perception and synthesis. The approach matters because the region identified from a user’s reference becomes part of the learned editing pipeline, tying what the model understands to where it generates changes.
neurips-2025-focus-unified-vision-langua.tldr: FOCUS jointly learns object localization and image generation so that language-guided understanding can directly guide controllable editing.

paragraphs: Flow-based generators can produce high-quality samples, but inference requires solving a differential equation. Consistency models seek to accelerate this process by learning its solution operator, or flow map. This paper develops a common framework for learning that map directly, making the relationships among different training methods explicit.

The framework connects the continuous flow’s velocity field to the instantaneous change of its flow map. Using that relationship, the authors show how distillation schemes can become direct training algorithms through self-distillation, removing the need for pretrained teachers. They organize methods into Eulerian, Lagrangian, and Progressive families based on different mathematical descriptions of the same map.

These families encompass and extend known distillation and direct-training approaches. The new Lagrangian methods avoid spatial derivatives and bootstrapping from small steps by design, and the authors find that they train more stably and perform better than standard Eulerian and Progressive alternatives. The framework therefore offers both a unifying explanation and concrete design principles for faster generative models.
neurips-2025-how-to-build-a-consistency-.tldr: A unified flow-map framework enables teacher-free consistency-model training and identifies Lagrangian methods with improved stability and performance.

paragraphs: Embodied AI needs simulated environments that reflect the diversity and clutter of actual indoor spaces. Existing scene datasets can be small, lack variety, omit small objects, or contain severe object collisions. InternScenes brings together real-world scans, procedurally generated environments, and designer-created scenes to provide a larger and more varied collection.

The dataset contains approximately 40,000 scenes and 1.96 million 3D objects, covering 15 scene types and 288 object classes. It retains many small items, with an average of 41.5 objects per region. Processing converts scans into simulation-ready replicas, adds interactive objects, and uses physical simulation to resolve collisions, making the detailed layouts usable for embodied tasks.

The authors demonstrate the dataset through scene layout generation and navigation to a specified point. Both applications expose challenges introduced by complex, realistic arrangements. They also show how the collection supports scaling training for these tasks, enabling generation and navigation in such environments. Its value lies in combining scene scale with preserved complexity and practical simulatability.
neurips-2025-internscenes-a-large-scale-.tldr: InternScenes provides about 40,000 simulation-ready indoor scenes that preserve clutter and support training for layout generation and navigation.

paragraphs: Meta-learning trains a system to adapt quickly to new tasks. Its episodic training setup already identifies which task each episode belongs to, but that information can provide additional supervision beyond the ordinary training objective. This paper uses task identity to help shape what a meta-learner learns across episodes.

ConML introduces a contrastive meta-objective operating on model representations. The goal is to use alignment and discrimination informed by task identity to improve generalization. By contrasting the representations learned by meta-learners, the method adds supervision at the level of the learning process itself. The framework is designed to work across different problems and types of learners.

The authors demonstrate integration with existing meta-learning methods and with in-context learning models, reporting substantial performance gains at a small implementation cost. The significance is that useful supervision is already present in the episodic organization of training. ConML turns that task information into an explicit objective that can complement existing approaches to learning how to adapt.
neurips-2025-learning-to-learn-with-cont.tldr: ConML uses task identity to contrast learned model representations, improving meta-learning and in-context learning with little implementation overhead.

paragraphs: A useful language-model router must balance whether a model can answer a query with how much using it costs. LLMRec treats this choice as a recommendation problem: the suitability of a model for a query is a hidden preference signal to be learned. It selects a candidate without first running inference on the candidate models.

The system combines model attributes and capability distributions with query meaning, additional query characteristics, and context such as inference type and budget. Behavioral features help it learn more complex interactions among these factors. Its design also targets unfamiliar datasets and newly added models, addressing the changing set of choices available to a routing system.

Evaluation considers the accuracy-cost Pareto frontier under user-specified budgets. Across six datasets, LLMRec reports an average cost reduction exceeding 38% while maintaining accuracy and outperforming baselines in approaching that frontier. The findings support learning which model suits each request as a practical way to reduce spending without sacrificing measured answer quality.
neurips-2025-let-the-llm-stick-to-its-st.tldr: LLMRec recommends a suitable language model for each query and budget, reporting over 38% average cost savings while maintaining accuracy.

paragraphs: Some dynamical systems depend strongly on their history. Fractional differential equations provide a way to represent such memory, but existing fractional neural models commonly assign historical states fixed weights. That rigidity makes it difficult to adapt memory use to the particular context of a prediction. FADE introduces learned attention into this historical weighting.

The model replaces fixed kernels in fractional operators with neural attention kernels. Historical states can therefore receive different emphasis according to their relevance to the current prediction. This combines the memory structure of fractional calculus with context-dependent selection, allowing the model to emphasize useful temporal dependencies and reduce the influence of less relevant history.

The theoretical analysis establishes bounded solutions, well-posedness, and convergence properties for the numerical solver. Experiments cover fluid flow, graph learning, and spatiotemporal traffic forecasting, where FADE outperforms both integer-order neural ODE models and existing fractional approaches. Together, the analysis and evaluations support adaptive historical weighting as a useful approach to dynamics with varying temporal dependencies.
neurips-2025-neural-fractional-attention.tldr: FADE combines fractional differential equations with learned attention so that dynamical models can adapt how they use historical information.

paragraphs: The median-of-means estimator is used to estimate averages robustly, and its optimality is established for independent, identically distributed samples. The paper studies a harsher setting: an adversary can inspect the data and change observations. Beyond Gaussian distributions, it was unclear when this estimator remains optimal and where its robustness falls short.

The authors derive upper and lower error bounds across several distribution classes. They show minimax optimality for distributions with finite variance and also for an infinite-variance class with a finite absolute moment of order 1+r. Minimax optimality concerns the best achievable worst-case error over the specified class, so these results depend on which distributions are allowed.

Matching-order lower bounds characterize the estimator’s error, while another result establishes that it is suboptimal for light-tailed distributions. The findings therefore identify both a strength and a real boundary: median-of-means can attain the optimal worst-case rate under adversarial contamination for broad moment-defined classes, yet fail to be optimal for a lighter-tailed class.
neurips-2025-on-the-optimality-of-the-me.tldr: Median-of-means is minimax optimal under adversarial contamination for specified moment classes, but suboptimal for light-tailed distributions.

paragraphs: Robot policies often generate several actions at once to maintain coherent movement. However, computing the next action sequence can take long enough to cause pauses or jerky transitions between chunks. Real-time chunking, or RTC, changes inference so that producing a new chunk overlaps with executing the current one.

RTC preserves actions that are already guaranteed to execute and fills in the remaining actions through inpainting. This lets the next sequence account for commitments already made during the computation delay. The method applies to diffusion- or flow-based vision-language-action policies without retraining, making execution timing the focus of the intervention rather than a new policy-training procedure.

The authors introduce twelve highly dynamic simulation tasks and also evaluate six real-world two-arm manipulation tasks. Results show higher throughput and strong robustness to inference delays, including successful precise actions such as lighting a match under extreme latency. These findings demonstrate that coordinating generation with ongoing execution can improve practical control even when model inference remains slow.
neurips-2025-real-time-execution-of-acti.tldr: RTC overlaps action generation with execution, smoothing robot control and improving robustness to inference delays without retraining.

paragraphs: Polarization images contain physical information useful for tasks such as separating reflections and identifying materials. Acquiring them usually requires additional optical hardware. This paper introduces RGB-to-polarization estimation as a task that instead predicts polarization information from ordinary color images, seeking to reduce the cost and complexity of obtaining useful estimates.

The authors assemble a benchmark using existing polarization datasets and evaluate a range of deep learning approaches. These include restoration-oriented models and generative architectures, allowing comparison between direct reconstruction and synthesis. The study also examines task-specific training alongside large-scale pretraining, using both quantitative measurements and qualitative inspection to assess their strengths and limitations.

A central constraint is that polarization information is fundamentally absent from standard RGB measurements, so the task involves inference from available visual evidence. The benchmark establishes the current performance level of the evaluated methods and outlines possible research directions. Its contribution is a shared basis for designing and assessing future estimators, rather than a claim that ordinary images directly measure polarization.
neurips-2025-rgb-to-polarization-estimat.tldr: A new benchmark evaluates how well restoration and generative models can infer polarization information from standard RGB images.

paragraphs: Learning to predict good solutions can accelerate mixed-integer linear programming, but models trained within one problem domain often struggle elsewhere. RoME targets this transfer problem with a mixture of specialized experts. Learned task representations determine which experts receive each problem instance, allowing a single model to handle varied optimization domains.

Training uses distributionally robust optimization at two levels. Across domains, it addresses broad shifts in problem distributions. Within domains, perturbations to task representations encourage local robustness. The authors find that learning across domains can also improve performance inside individual domains, suggesting that shared training helps capture combinatorial patterns useful beyond a single problem family.

A model trained on three domains reports an average improvement of 67.7% when evaluated on five domains. The abstract does not identify that percentage with a specific performance measure. Further zero-shot evaluation on MIPLIB shows measurable gains on challenging real-world instances. These results support domain-aware specialization combined with robust training as a route toward more transferable learned solution prediction.
neurips-2025-rome-domain-robust-mixture-.tldr: RoME combines specialized experts with robustness training across and within domains to improve transferable MILP solution prediction.

paragraphs: Pseudo-labeling uses a model’s predictions as training targets for unlabeled examples. In regression, those predictions are continuous, and their noise can vary from example to example. This heteroscedastic uncertainty makes reliability harder to judge than in classification. Treating unreliable predictions as trustworthy targets can accumulate errors and encourage overfitting.

The proposed framework adjusts the influence of pseudo-labels using learned uncertainty. It formulates the process as a bi-level optimization problem: one level minimizes empirical error across the available data, while another optimizes uncertainty estimates to improve generalization on labeled data. This ties the weight assigned to predicted labels to their usefulness for learning from known targets.

The paper provides theoretical insights and evaluates the approach on several semi-supervised regression benchmarks. Results show improved robustness and performance compared with existing methods. The main contribution is a principled way to control how much a learner trusts its own predictions when label quality varies, allowing unlabeled examples to contribute without giving unreliable pseudo-labels equal influence.
neurips-2025-semi-supervised-regression-.tldr: Uncertainty-aware bi-level optimization adjusts pseudo-label influence to improve semi-supervised regression when prediction noise varies across examples.

paragraphs: Distributed training can reduce communication by compressing gradients, while adaptive optimizers can improve the optimization process. Combining them complicates analysis because compression affects both first- and second-moment estimates, which interact through a ratio. Existing theoretical challenges also include avoiding strong dependence on parameter count and guaranteeing behavior beyond average outcomes.

SADL is a family of algorithms combining suitable unbiased gradient sketches with suitable adaptive optimizers. Its convergence analysis handles both moment approximations and provides high-probability guarantees. Dependence on the total parameter count is only logarithmic, while the treatment of moment error introduces dependence on the loss Hessian’s intrinsic dimension, described as much smaller than the full model dimension.

Experiments cover vision and language tasks, both training from scratch and supervised fine-tuning. SADL is competitive with, and often exceeds, the tested baselines, including strong communication-efficient methods using error feedback. The contribution pairs practical compressed adaptive training with sharper guarantees that address large model size and variability in convergence.
neurips-2025-sketched-adaptive-distribut.tldr: SADL combines gradient sketching with adaptive optimization and supplies high-probability convergence guarantees with only logarithmic dependence on parameter count.

paragraphs: Personalized dialogue requires a model to learn about a user over time, including when little is known initially. The paper argues that static prompting and offline optimization are limited in these cold-start and long-term settings. RLPA trains a language model to infer and revise user profiles through repeated dialogue with a simulated user.

Training has two reward levels. A profile reward encourages accurate representations of the user, while a response reward encourages answers consistent with that inferred profile. This makes maintaining a useful understanding of the user an explicit training objective alongside producing suitable replies. The authors instantiate the framework by fine-tuning Qwen-2.5-3B-Instruct into Qwen-RLPA.

In the reported evaluations, Qwen-RLPA outperforms prompting and offline fine-tuning baselines, as well as Claude-3.5 and GPT-4o. Further analyses show strengths in handling conflicting preferences and sustaining personalization, with more efficient inference than recent reasoning-focused models. These findings support dynamic profile inference as a promising approach to personalization within the evaluated dialogue settings.
neurips-2025-teaching-language-models-to.tldr: RLPA trains language models to update user profiles through dialogue, improving personalized responses in the reported evaluations.

paragraphs: Sparse attention is often studied as a way to reduce transformer computation. This paper instead asks how sparsity affects learning and generalization. Across the studied mechanisms, attention that selects connections based on the current input appears to learn faster and generalize better, while input-independent sparsity shows no comparable benefit.

The authors interpret the useful form as semantic focus: concentrating attention according to the tokens being processed. They develop theory linking softmax stability to how sensitively the loss changes, then analyze how sparsity influences convergence and generalization guarantees. This separates the effects of merely removing attention connections from those of choosing connections using input information.

Within the theoretical characterization, input-independent sparsity provides no improvement, whereas input-dependent sparsity can improve guarantees under specified conditions. The experiments satisfy those conditions, and the observed pattern persists across architectural and optimization choices. The result is a conditional explanation of why some sparse attention designs help learning, beyond their potential savings in computation and memory.
neurips-2025-transformers-learn-faster-w.tldr: Input-dependent sparse attention can improve transformer learning and generalization under characterized conditions, unlike sparsity chosen independently of the input.

paragraphs: Discrete diffusion generates samples by reversing a process that corrupts data. Although gradual denoising offers ways to incorporate useful structure, masking diffusion has performed especially well despite not denoising gradually. The paper explains this advantage through how discrete Markov processes change: they move through discontinuous jumps with a known distribution of jump times.

Masking diffusion incorporates that timing distribution and learns where the jumps should go. The authors show how to incorporate the known timing distribution into other discrete diffusion models as well. The resulting schedule-conditioned diffusion framework, SCUD, generalizes both classical discrete diffusion and masking diffusion, separating known jump timing from the transitions that must be learned.

The authors apply SCUD to noising processes containing inductive biases for images, text, and proteins. The resulting models outperform masking diffusion in their evaluations. This supports the proposed explanation while showing a practical consequence: incorporating jump schedules can preserve the advantages of structured noising processes and improve on masking in the studied applications.
neurips-2025-why-masking-diffusion-works.tldr: SCUD incorporates known jump-time distributions into discrete diffusion, enabling structured models that outperform masking diffusion in the reported evaluations.
